newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Philips, unions end Hoogeveen dispute.
newsitem.headline: Philips, unions end Hoogeveen dispute.

text.p: Philips Electronics NV said on Monday it had reached agreement with unions at its Hoogeveen plant about phased job cuts as it transfers some of the plant's production to Poland.
Workers at the plant in the eastern Netherlands went on strike a week ago in protest at restructuring at the plant, demanding that no jobs be lost in the production transfer.

A Philips spokesman said on Monday that under a new agreement 250-275 workers would be guaranteed work through a yet to be identified employment agency for three years as the company moves their production functions to Poland.

The spokesman said some production from the plant, which employs 850 people to make vacuum cleaners, coffee machines and kitchen appliances, would move in three steps planned for August this year, the turn of the year and summer 1998.
"The unions wanted a guarantee of no job losses and this was the maximum effort to prevent reductions," he said.

"There's a guarantee of work for three years but that's up to the employment organisation to work out. The experts say that they can solve that problem," he added. A statement said the jobs with the agency would be on compatible terms to those they hold at Philips.
